experiment: HIPPARCHUS against IRSA's own SPHEREx tools, on the same exposures
claim: consistency check only; IRSA's tools are references, not ground truth

local_changes: __init__.py replaced by an empty file (upstream imports bokeh/firefly/SExtractor helpers we do not call)
fetch_sapm() replaced: the same cal-sapm-v3-2026-191 maps, read over HTTPS from IRSA instead of anonymous S3, and only for the detectors we need; the interpolator is still the SDT's interp2d_rg

settings.background: sigma-clipped median in annulus (SDT's extract_photometry); no flag masking in the aperture sum
settings.spectral_wcs: WCS(key='W') with sip=None, as the notebook

method_differences_vs_hipparchus: Aperture: SDT r=3 px (notebook) vs ours r=2 px; we also run SDT at r=2 px.
Background: SDT sigma-clipped median of a 7-16 px annulus vs our plain median of a 4-7 px annulus with flagged pixels excluded.
Flags: SDT sums all pixels and only counts flags afterwards; we refuse a measurement when any aperture pixel carries a BAD_PLANES flag.
Units: SDT converts to mJy with the solid angle pixel map; ours is MJy/sr summed over pixels. We convert ours with the map value at the target's detector pixel.

Solid angle position: the SDT interpolates the full-detector map at cutout pixel indices (its sa_mjy_scale_map), i.e. the detector corner, not the cutout's real place. We report SDT verbatim and with that factor corrected (omegafixed).
Grid: our epoch b is measured after reprojection onto epoch a's grid; SDT measures every exposure on its own grid.
Wavelength: SDT reads WCS-WAVE without SIP; our published numbers use the legacy 'wcs' source (SIP applied, see quality.WAVELENGTH_SOURCES).

target.name: RW Aurigae
target.why: Young star known to vary; unsaturated in detector 1, so a real comparison is possible.

target.name: WISE 0855-0714
target.why: The coldest known brown dwarf: faint, so this tests the limit of the data.

spectrophotometry_tool.tool: IRSA SPHEREx Spectrophotometry Tool (Tractor forced PSF photometry, SPHEREx Data Explorer)
spectrophotometry_tool.reason: GUI-only as documented: jobs are submitted from the SPHEREx Data Explorer web app and tracked in its Job Monitor (UWS under the hood, but no public endpoint or parameter list is documented); IRSA's SPHEREx API list covers SIA v2 and the cutout service only. Each job also takes >= 5 min and is throttled to 2 per user. We did not reverse-engineer the web app, so there are no Tractor numbers in this file.
spectrophotometry_tool.how_to_run_by_hand: SPHEREx Data Explorer -> Spectrophotometry -> Point Source at RA 76.956, Dec +30.401 (RW Aur) and RA 133.76, Dec -7.2424 (WISE 0855); download the table and match its lvf_id/det_id/mjd columns to the obs ids in the evidence files.
expected_differences_if_run: PSF fit (Tractor, measured PSF) vs our 2 px aperture: no aperture loss, so absolute fluxes should be higher than ours by the inverse of our encircled-energy fraction.
Background from flag-masked nearby pixels fitted jointly vs our median 4-7 px annulus.
uJy via the pixel solid angle map vs our MJy/sr summed over pixels (cancels in ratios).

interpretation: RW Aur, same aperture (r=2 px), same 10 exposures: SDT/ours = 0.9998 (robust scatter 0.0040). On exposures we measure on their own grid the median is 0.9979 (n=6); on exposures we measure after reprojection it is 1.0055 (n=4). So the background methods agree to a few 0.1%, and our bilinear reprojection of epoch b costs about 0.8% of its flux in a 2 px aperture.

RW Aur brightness ratios (8 published pairs): SDT ratio / our ratio = 1.0093 (robust scatter 0.0037); the ~1% excess is the reprojection loss above, not a calibration difference. All 8 pairs are 'changed' in both. The SDT's significances are larger (median +18 sigma) because its error is the variance sum only, while ours adds the sky-level error for every aperture pixel.

As published (r=3 px, SDT's own solid-angle handling) SDT/ours = 1.0052: the larger aperture adds light, while the SDT reads the solid angle map at the detector corner instead of the cutout's real place, which here is 1.3% too small; the two partly cancel.

Wavelengths: SDT - ours = +1.4 nm median on D1 (max 1.8) and +3.7 nm on D6 (range -0.3 to 9.8). The SDT reads WCS-WAVE without SIP; our published numbers use the legacy 'wcs' source with SIP applied, the offset we already document (up to 18 nm on D6).

WISE 0855 (our S/N median 3.0): at r=2 px SDT/ours = 0.981 (robust scatter 0.215), (SDT - ours)/sigma_ours median -0.06. No pair is 'changed' for either at r=2 px (27/27 verdicts agree). At r=3 px, as published, the SDT calls 3 pairs changed; every one involves an exposure with flagged pixels inside its aperture, which the SDT sums and only counts afterwards (7 exposures). Those pixels lie between 2 and 3 px from the target (0 exposures are flagged at r=2 px), so our 2 px aperture never touches them, and we would refuse the measurement if it did.

MOST lists 36 SPHEREx images with (216) Kleopatra in the window; we used 38. 36 are common, 0 are MOST-only, 2 are ours-only (2025W25_1B_0393_1): there the predicted position is beyond the detector edge, we flagged it 'off_edge' and measured nothing, so both tools agree it is not in the image.

MOST positions equal Horizons as seen from SPHEREx at the exposure START (rms 0.0013 arcsec), not at mid-exposure (0.27 arcsec) and not geocentric (1.53 arcsec). Against our measured centroids MOST differs by 0.33 arcsec median (n=31), mostly that start-vs-mid time offset; both are far below the 6.15 arcsec pixel.
The Spectrophotometry Tool (Tractor PSF photometry) was NOT RUN: see spectrophotometry_tool.reason.
